subject.title: Feature: Activity-aware run timeout (wall-clock timeout kills active multi-tool runs)

question: Should OpenClaw replace the current single wall-clock chat/agent run deadline with activity-aware idle timeout plus a hard max-run cap, and how should that map onto existing `agents.defaults.timeoutSeconds`?
rationale: The remaining work changes core runtime semantics and likely config/default behavior, can extend resource usage, and overlaps with narrower open PRs that do not settle the product contract.

options.title: Define idle plus hard cap
options.body: Choose the idle-vs-hard-cap contract first, then request or review a focused implementation that keeps safety and user-visible timeout reporting together.

options.title: Land only narrow mitigations
options.body: Review #89965 and #95536 as separate fixes while keeping this issue open for broader run-budget semantics.

options.title: Keep wall-clock semantics
options.body: Treat the 48-hour default plus explicit timeout configuration as sufficient and close or narrow this issue to timeout messaging only.

recommendation.title: Define idle plus hard cap
recommendation.body: Choose the idle-vs-hard-cap contract first, then request or review a focused implementation that keeps safety and user-visible timeout reporting together.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision crosses gateway active-run state, embedded-runner liveness, and config policy, and this is the strongest available routing signal from the relevant history.
